newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-PASTRANA STRIPPED OF IBF JUNIOR FLYWEIGHT TITLE.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-PASTRANA STRIPPED OF IBF JUNIOR FLYWEIGHT TITLE.

text.p: The International Boxing Federation on Wednesday declared its junior flyweight title vacant, stripping Mauricio Pastrana of the belt for failing to attend a weigh-in for a May 10 title defence.
The Colombian was scheduled to fight Manuel Herrara in Coconut Grove, Florida, last Saturday, but instead of turning up for Friday's weigh-in, he sent word through a representative that he was ill.

IBF President Bob Lee said in a news release that the Florida Commission sent a doctor to Pastrana's room to examine the champion and the doctor declared him fit to fight, despite Pastrana's complaints of pain in his testicles.

IBF rules state that a fighter must appear at a weigh-in for a title bout unless he notifies the sanctioning body with a doctor's certificate that he is unable to fight. When Pastrana declined to appear, he effectively forfeited his title, the IBF said.
"Pastrana is a fine boxer and there would be no hesitation on our part to let him fight for the title again, provided he adheres to the rules governing a champion's activity," Lee said.
